title: Power Apps: prompt columns can store multiple lines of text output
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, consumption licensing and prompt-column controls are supported. Microsoft pages differ on the heading containing the environment AI prompts setting; the control note should acknowledge that navigation difference.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans multiple lines of prompt output, enabling longer and more detailed AI-generated text in tables.
claims.quote: Prompt columns can now store multilple lines of text as prompt output, enabling longer and detailed AI-generated insights to be stored in your tables.

claims.claim: The item lists Power Apps and Microsoft Dataverse.

claims.claim: Prompt columns hold results from natural-language prompts tied to other columns in the table.
claims.quote: enables you to define natural language prompts tied to other columns in your table. The AI model processes these prompts to generate relevant responses based on specified input columns.

claims.claim: A prompt executes on record creation.

claims.claim: Generated prompt-column results persist as table data.
claims.quote: The key function is that the prompt column contains generative AI results stored in the table persistently.

claims.claim: The prompt columns Learn page does not describe multiple-line output at the time of writing.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps prompt columns multiline output 573279 licensing price default rollout switch; read prompt-column and roadmap. Learn describes existing columns upgrading to asynchronous execution, but does not tie that to multiple-line output.

claims.claim: A length limit for stored multiple-line prompt output is not yet documented.

claims.claim: No new administrator switch specifically for multiple-line output is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multiple lines" output default length admin enable; read prompt-column, administer, settings-features and organization reference; found general AI prompts controls, not a multiline-specific switch.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls: monitoring
claims.claim: The AI Builder activity report is under Automation center in Power Automate.
claims.quote: Sign in to Power Automate. On the left navigation pane, select Automation center, and then select AI Builder activity.

claims.claim: The report's Estimated consumption column shows credits consumed per prompt execution.
claims.quote: Review the Estimated consumption column to see the credits consumed by each prompt execution.

claims.claim: Filter conditions reduce unnecessary prompt executions and help optimise credit consumption.
claims.quote: During record creation or update, the prompt column evaluates the filter first and then executes the prompt for eligible records. This approach reduces unnecessary executions and helps optimize Copilot credit consumption.

claims.claim: Input tokens contribute to prompt-run cost.
claims.quote: The combination of input tokens, output tokens, and the model version allows you to compute the cost of your prompt run.

claims.claim: Output tokens contribute to prompt-run cost.
claims.quote: The combination of input tokens, output tokens, and the model version allows you to compute the cost of your prompt run.

claims.claim: The prompt columns prerequisites require the environment's Copilot feature to be on.
claims.quote: Copilot and AI Prompts features turned On in the Features area for the environment settings.

claims.claim: The prompt columns prerequisites require the environment's AI Prompts feature to be on.
claims.quote: Copilot and AI Prompts features turned On in the Features area for the environment settings.

claims.claim: A table can have up to five prompt columns.
claims.quote: You can create up to five prompt columns per table.

claims.claim: Block unmanaged customizations must be disabled to create or edit prompt columns.
claims.quote: To create or edit Prompt Columns, the‘Block unmanaged customizations’ environment setting must be disabled.

claims.claim: Updating feature settings requires the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions.
claims.quote: Ensure you have the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions to update the settings.

claims.claim: The general AI prompts feature is enabled by default.
claims.quote: By default, the AI prompts feature is enabled for makers to create and experiment with various AI-generated content.

claims.claim: The environment control is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > AI Builder > AI prompts.
claims.quote: select Environments > [select an environment] > Settings > Product > Features. On the Features settings page under AI Builder, enable or disable the AI prompts toggle.
claims.fix: Append to controls[0].note: 'Administer AI Builder places this toggle under AI Builder; Manage feature settings lists it under AI prompts (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/settings-features#ai-prompts).' The latter page also confirms the initial Manage > Environments steps.

claims.claim: PATCH /api/data/v9.2/organizations(<organizationid>) updates the organization record for this environment setting.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations; Primary key: organizationid; Operations supported: GETPATCH

claims.claim: The request body sets aipromptsenabled to true or false.
claims.quote: aipromptsenabled | Edm.Boolean | Indicates whether AI Prompts feature is enabled.

claims.claim: The environment AI prompts control governs prompt-column execution.
claims.quote: Why didn't the prompt column execute? Common scenarios where the prompt doesn't execute, no error is surfaced, and execution is skipped: AI Prompt feature is disabled.

claims.claim: An AI prompts environment-group rule can govern AI prompts availability for the group's environments.
claims.quote: If your environment is part of an environment group, you can also govern AI prompts feature availability through the AI prompts environment group rule.

claims.claim: Publishing an AI prompts group rule locks the environment setting, requiring changes through the group rule.
claims.quote: If an environment group rule governing AI prompts is published, it locks the AI prompts setting at the environment-level, preventing any system administrator of those individual environments from editing the setting.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second row; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The per-column control is at Power Apps (maker) > Tables > table > Columns > column > Edit column > Allow prompt column execution.
claims.quote: Select Tables on the left navigation pane. Open the table, select Columns, and then open the column that is of data type Prompt where you want to disable AI generation. On the Edit column pane, clear the Allow prompt column execution checkbox

claims.claim: Allow prompt column execution is enabled by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Allow prompt column execution setting is enabled.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].note; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Disabling Allow prompt column execution prevents AI analysis for that individual prompt column.
claims.quote: When disabled, AI analysis isn't performed for the prompt column.

claims.claim: An API or command for Allow prompt column execution is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Allow prompt column execution" API attribute metadata Dataverse; "prompt column" "execution" API PowerShell CLI attribute enabled; read prompt-column, specialized-columns and msdyn_aiconfiguration reference; no setting operation found.

claims.claim: Learn says both tenant-level and column-level settings must be enabled for prompts to execute.
claims.quote: For prompts to be executed, both tenant level and column level settings need to be enabled.

claims.claim: Insufficient permission on a referenced input column is a documented cause of prompt-column generation failure.
claims.quote: The user doesn't have sufficient permissions on one or more input columns referenced in the prompt column definition.

claims.claim: The roadmap description mentions no new connector, identity or permission.
claims.quote: Prompt columns can now store multilple lines of text as prompt output, enabling longer and detailed AI-generated insights to be stored in your tables.

claims.claim: Learn states on-demand prompt-column execution is not currently supported.
claims.quote: Prompt columns are triggered automatically on record updates; however, on‑demand execution is not currently supported.

claims.claim: The prompts overview advises human review before using generated content to inform a business decision.

claims.claim: Prompt columns are not audited.

claims.claim: The corresponding columns record execution status.

claims.claim: The corresponding Details column records execution failure details.

claims.claim: Status and Details columns can be added to the displayed table columns to monitor execution.
claims.quote: In the select Show existing column list search for the prompt column name. Search and select the columns named: (columnName) _PromptColumnStatus; (columnName)_PromptColumnDetails

claims.claim: Learn does not specifically tie the general AI prompts and per-column execution controls to multiple-line output.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multiple lines" output default length admin enable; read prompt-column, administer and settings-features; controls govern prompts generally, with no multiple-line-specific description.

claims.claim: Prompt runs consume AI credit capacity associated with their environment.
claims.quote: Once an environment has Copilot Credits available, it can run the AI Builder features in all contexts. If an environment only has AI Builder credits available, it can only run AI Builder features in Power Apps and Power Automate.
